paragraphs: AlpacaFarm makes it cheaper to study how language models learn to follow instructions from feedback. This research normally requires collecting human judgments, deciding how to evaluate the resulting models, and implementing training methods reliably. The paper brings these pieces together in a simulation framework intended to support experimentation on the full workflow.

The framework uses a language model to simulate human feedback, reporting high agreement with people at 45 times lower cost than crowdworkers. It also supplies an instruction evaluation dataset, an automatic evaluation procedure, and reference implementations of methods that learn from pairwise preferences. These include PPO, best-of-n, and expert iteration, allowing researchers to compare approaches within a shared setup.

For validation, the authors train and evaluate eleven models using 10,000 pairs of human feedback. Model rankings from the simulator match those from training on human data in this comparison. They also find that reward-model-based methods can substantially improve on supervised fine-tuning. These results support AlpacaFarm as a useful experimental proxy for the feedback-learning workflows studied.
neurips-2023-alpacafarm-a-simulation-fra.tldr: AlpacaFarm provides inexpensive simulated feedback, evaluation tools, and reference methods whose model rankings match human-feedback training in the reported validation.

paragraphs: Beta diffusion introduces a generative process designed for data whose values lie within bounded ranges. It combines removing masks with removing noise, using scaled and shifted beta distributions. Its transitions are multiplicative, providing a different mathematical construction from diffusion methods that progressively add Gaussian noise.

The construction preserves beta distributions in the forward marginals and in reverse conditional distributions when conditioned on the data. The paper also changes how the model is trained. It derives upper bounds on KL divergence, called KLUBs, from the convexity of that divergence and uses these bounds as optimization objectives.

The authors show that KLUB objectives are more effective for training beta diffusion than negative evidence lower bounds. Their analysis connects the objectives through swapping the arguments of the underlying KL divergence and expresses the loss using Bregman divergence. Experiments on synthetic data and natural images support both the bounded-data modeling approach and the proposed training objectives. The contribution therefore concerns the diffusion process itself and the objective used to learn it.
neurips-2023-beta-diffusion-d75fdbd9a7.tldr: Beta diffusion uses multiplicative beta-distributed transitions and KL-divergence upper-bound objectives to generate data within bounded ranges.

paragraphs: Brain encoding models predict measured brain responses from representations of what a person experiences. Such models usually treat language and vision separately, even though both can convey related concepts. This paper asks whether representations from transformers trained on multiple modalities can support predictions that transfer between language and visual experiences.

The researchers use multimodal transformer representations to train encoding models on fMRI responses to stories and movies. They find that a model trained on responses to one modality can predict responses to the other. This transfer is particularly successful in cortical regions associated with conceptual meaning, connecting the predictive results to representations of meaning shared across the two kinds of input.

Further analysis identifies shared semantic dimensions underlying language and vision representations. Comparisons with encoding models built from unimodal transformers indicate that multimodal transformers learn more aligned conceptual representations. Together, these findings show how multimodal models can help investigate the brain’s processing of meaning across different sensory and linguistic formats.
neurips-2023-brain-encoding-models-based.tldr: Encoding models built from multimodal transformers transfer between brain responses to stories and movies, revealing shared representations of conceptual meaning.

paragraphs: Adding image understanding to a language model can require training many parameters and performing another large pre-training stage before instruction tuning. This paper proposes Mixture-of-Modality Adaptation, or MMA, as an affordable way to adapt language models to tasks involving both images and text.

MMA uses lightweight adapters to connect image and language processing, enabling joint optimization of the image and language models. It also includes a routing algorithm that switches between text-only and multimodal instructions while preserving natural-language understanding. Applied to LLaMA, this approach produces the vision-language instruction model LaVIN.

The authors evaluate LaVIN on multimodal science question answering and dialogue. They report competitive performance alongside better training efficiency than existing multimodal language models, with a reported training run taking 1.4 hours and updating 3.8 million parameters. The findings support lightweight adaptation as a practical route to multimodal instruction following, while the dialogue experiments indicate potential for a general-purpose chatbot. The efficiency result makes the adaptation mechanism a central contribution alongside the model’s task performance.
neurips-2023-cheap-and-quick-efficient-v.tldr: MMA equips LLaMA with vision-language instruction following through lightweight adapters and modality routing, yielding competitive results with efficient training.

paragraphs: Color helps convolutional neural networks recognize objects, but recording conditions can make some color variations much more common in training than others. This imbalance can undermine performance when colors change. Simply making a model ignore color addresses that sensitivity at the cost of discarding potentially useful visual evidence.

The paper introduces Color Equivariant Convolutions, or CEConvs, which share shape features across different hues while retaining color information. The mechanism shares network parameters over hue shifts. This extends equivariance from changes in geometry to changes in appearance: the model handles specified color transformations in a structured way instead of removing color from its representation.

The authors report improvements in downstream tasks and greater robustness to color changes, including shifts between training and test distributions. CEConvs can be incorporated into existing architectures such as ResNets. The results support treating color variation as structure that a network can explicitly accommodate, allowing it to reuse shape knowledge while keeping the discriminative information that color provides.
neurips-2023-color-equivariant-convoluti.tldr: Color Equivariant Convolutions share features across hue shifts while preserving useful color information, improving robustness in the reported evaluations.

paragraphs: CommonScenes generates controllable 3D indoor environments from scene graphs, which compactly describe objects and their relationships. The paper addresses inconsistencies that can arise when generation methods overlook how objects relate to the overall scene and to one another. Its aim is to produce diverse shapes that also fit coherently into a scene.

The model has two branches. A variational autoencoder predicts the scene layout, while a latent diffusion model generates compatible object shapes. Both global scene-object relationships and local relationships between objects guide generation. Users can change the resulting environment by editing the input graph or varying the noise used by the diffusion model.

The authors also construct SG-FRONT by adding scene graph annotations to 3D-FRONT, addressing the need for data that combines object-level meshes with relationships. Experiments on SG-FRONT show advantages over other methods in consistency, quality, and diversity. These findings support jointly considering scene structure and object generation when building environments that are both editable and semantically coherent.
neurips-2023-commonscenes-generating-com.tldr: CommonScenes combines scene-layout prediction and shape diffusion to generate editable 3D interiors with improved consistency, quality, and diversity on SG-FRONT.

paragraphs: Many generative models work in a compressed latent space and use a decoder to turn latent representations into data. The choice of latent space strongly affects performance, but choosing it is not straightforward. This paper studies that choice through the complexity required of the generator.

Starting from the GAN training objective, the authors define a distance between latent and data distributions whose minimization coincides with minimizing generator complexity. Within this formulation, the best data-dependent latent distribution makes effective use of the generator’s capacity. They turn this idea into a training method called the Decoupled Autoencoder: first train the encoder with an auxiliary decoder, then freeze the encoder while training the actual decoder.

Separating these stages allows the learned latent distribution to shape the subsequent decoder-training problem. Experiments with models including VQGAN and Diffusion Transformer support the theoretical analysis, reporting significant improvements in sample quality together with reduced model complexity. The findings suggest that improving the latent representation can make generation easier, rather than relying solely on increasing the generator’s capacity.
neurips-2023-complexity-matters-rethinki.tldr: A complexity-based analysis motivates training and freezing the encoder before the final decoder, improving reported sample quality with lower model complexity.

paragraphs: Differentiable physics simulators can help optimize movements for manipulating deformable objects. With a suitable objective, a gradient-based solver can quickly find a valid trajectory. The difficulty is specifying that objective: translating a desired manipulation into the right mathematical conditions usually requires expertise.

DiffVL lets non-expert users describe soft-body manipulation tasks through visual information and natural language, including tasks with multiple stages. Large language models translate these descriptions into optimization objectives that a differentiable physics solver can use. This connects a user’s description of the intended result to the mathematical formulation needed for trajectory optimization.

The researchers develop graphical tools with which non-experts specify 100 tasks inspired by real-life manipulation videos, and state that these tasks will be made public. The generated objectives help solvers tackle long-horizon, multistage tasks that challenge previous baselines. The contribution is therefore both an interface for collecting naturalistic tasks and a translation method that makes those tasks accessible to physics-based optimization.
neurips-2023-diffvl-scaling-up-soft-body.tldr: DiffVL translates visual and natural-language task descriptions into objectives that help differentiable physics solvers perform multistage soft-body manipulation.

paragraphs: Sparse linear regression seeks a predictive relationship involving only a small subset of many features. This paper considers correlated Gaussian features, where relationships among inputs can make learning computationally difficult. Although strong recovery is information-theoretically possible from relatively few samples, efficient methods can need many more when the covariance matrix is poorly conditioned.

The authors give a polynomial-time algorithm that uses the known covariance matrix to adapt the Lasso to a small number of approximate dependencies among features. This targets a specific source of difficulty: even one sparse approximate dependency can substantially increase the samples required by classical methods. For constant sparsity and covariance matrices with few outlier eigenvalues, the proposed method achieves near-optimal sample complexity.

The algorithm belongs to a broader feature-adaptation framework for ill-conditioned inputs. That framework also yields a polynomial-factor improvement over brute-force search for constant sparsity and arbitrary covariance. The results distinguish favorable covariance structures, where strong sample guarantees are possible, from the broader setting, where the stated advance is a computational improvement.
neurips-2023-feature-adaptation-for-spar.tldr: Using known covariance structure, feature adaptation improves sparse regression under approximate dependencies and accelerates search for arbitrary covariance at constant sparsity.

paragraphs: Graph anomaly detection identifies unusual nodes using information about the nodes and their connections. Both traditional algorithms and graph neural networks have been developed for this task, but their relative performance and efficiency are difficult to judge without a shared evaluation setting. GADBench provides such a setting for supervised anomaly detection on static graphs.

The benchmark compares 29 models across ten real-world datasets. These graphs range from thousands of nodes to roughly six million, allowing the comparison to cover substantially different scales. Its focus includes whether specialized graph neural networks outperform traditional methods such as tree ensembles, as well as how efficiently methods handle large graphs.

The main finding is that tree ensembles supplied with simple neighborhood aggregation can outperform recent graph neural networks designed for anomaly detection. This shows that incorporating graph information does not always require a graph neural network to obtain strong results. The publicly released benchmark provides a common basis for evaluating future methods against both traditional and neural alternatives.
neurips-2023-gadbench-revisiting-and-ben.tldr: GADBench finds that tree ensembles with simple neighborhood aggregation can outperform specialized graph neural networks in supervised node anomaly detection.

paragraphs: Image segmentation normally requires detailed labels indicating which object or category each pixel belongs to. Sparse annotations reduce that labeling burden, but leave a model to infer much of the image structure. Pairwise affinity methods help by estimating which image locations belong together, often using similarities in nearby appearance.

This paper argues that local comparisons alone miss long-range dependencies and object topology. It formulates affinity modeling as a propagation process and combines local and global pairwise terms to produce soft pseudo labels. These inferred labels provide graded supervision where complete pixel-level annotations are unavailable. An accompanying efficient algorithm substantially reduces the computational cost of the proposed approach.

The method can be inserted into existing segmentation networks. Experiments cover box-supervised instance segmentation, point- or scribble-supervised semantic segmentation, and CLIP-guided semantic segmentation, with superior performance reported across these settings. The results support using broader relationships within an image to turn limited supervision into more informative training targets, rather than restricting affinity modeling to immediate neighbors.
neurips-2023-label-efficient-segmentatio.tldr: Combining local and global affinity propagation improves pseudo labels and segmentation performance across several forms of limited supervision.

paragraphs: Bilevel optimization links an outer decision problem to an inner optimization problem. Many existing nonconvex methods assume a fixed dataset and unchanging objectives. This paper studies an online version in which data arrive continuously and the objective functions can change, requiring the algorithm to keep updating its decisions.

The proposed method, SOBOW, uses a single update loop and averages recent estimates of the hypergradient, the information used to update the outer decision. Those estimates are stored in memory, so the algorithm can use their window average without needing access to previous objective functions. This design addresses both changing functions and the unavailability of exact hypergradients.

The analysis separates dependencies between decision variables and controls errors in the estimated hypergradients. Under mild conditions, SOBOW achieves sublinear bilevel local regret, meaning that this local-regret measure grows more slowly than the number of rounds. Experiments across multiple domains support its effectiveness. The theoretical contribution is a conditional online guarantee for a computationally efficient method in a changing optimization environment.
neurips-2023-non-convex-bilevel-optimiza.tldr: SOBOW averages recent hypergradient estimates to efficiently solve changing online bilevel problems, with sublinear local regret under mild conditions.

paragraphs: Logistic bandits model sequential decisions in which an action produces feedback governed by a logistic model. The binary version has two possible feedback outcomes, while the multinomial version supports more than two. This paper develops an algorithm that improves the balance between learning performance and the computation required at each decision round.

For binary feedback, the algorithm reduces per-round computation from logarithmic in the time horizon T to constant with respect to T. It retains a minimax-optimal guarantee up to logarithmic factors. This means its stated computational cost does not grow with the length of the interaction in the way the compared method’s cost does.

For K+1 feedback outcomes, the regret bound scales as K times the square root of T, ignoring logarithmic factors. This removes a square-root dependence on a potentially large parameter-domain constant from the previous tractable bound. Per-round computation also becomes constant with respect to T, compared with the previous linear dependence. These are simultaneous improvements in the statistical guarantee and horizon-dependent computational cost.
neurips-2023-online-multinomial-logistic.tldr: A logistic bandit algorithm improves multinomial regret guarantees while keeping per-round computation constant with respect to the time horizon.

paragraphs: This paper studies a seller who can offer multiple items to multiple users in each round. The seller must decide both who receives an offer and what price to charge, while initially lacking users’ valuations. Learning comes from whether each offer is accepted or rejected, linking revenue generation to information gathering.

The authors design online algorithms for three valuation models: fixed valuations, random experiences, and random valuations. Their guarantees depend on the number of users N, the number of items M, the number of rounds T, and market load L. Load roughly measures how many allocations can happen simultaneously, so the analysis explicitly accounts for the market’s allocation capacity.

Under fixed valuations, revenue regret has order O(NM log log(LT)). For both random models, the bound is of order square root of NMLT, up to logarithmic factors. The authors characterize these guarantees as nearly optimal. The results show how offering and pricing decisions can be coordinated while learning from limited feedback, with different rates reflecting the different valuation models.
neurips-2023-online-pricing-for-multi-us.tldr: Online offering and pricing algorithms learn valuations from accept/reject feedback with nearly optimal revenue regret across three multi-user, multi-item market models.

paragraphs: PointGPT adapts generative pre-training to point clouds, whose points do not naturally form an ordered sequence. The approach also addresses their low information density and the gap between pre-training and downstream tasks. Its core idea is to learn useful 3D representations by predicting successive portions of a point cloud.

The method divides a point cloud into patches and orders them by spatial proximity. An extractor-generator transformer with dual masking learns representations from preceding patches and predicts the next patch. To study scaling, the authors collect a larger pre-training dataset. They also introduce a subsequent training stage using a labeled hybrid dataset to improve downstream performance.

The reported results include classification accuracies of 94.9% on ModelNet40 and 93.4% on ScanObjectNN, outperforming the other transformer models in the comparison. PointGPT also achieves new state-of-the-art accuracies on all four evaluated few-shot benchmarks. These findings support autoregressive point-patch prediction as a scalable pre-training strategy that transfers to several 3D understanding tasks.
neurips-2023-pointgpt-auto-regressively-.tldr: PointGPT pre-trains transformers by predicting spatially ordered point-cloud patches, achieving strong classification and few-shot results.

paragraphs: Money laundering can involve complex transaction patterns across banks and countries, yet real transaction data for training detection models are generally unavailable. This paper addresses the need for a public, standardized way to compare anti-money-laundering models. It contributes both a synthetic transaction generator and datasets produced by that generator.

The generator is agent-based and calibrated to resemble real financial transactions as closely as possible. The authors describe how it works and demonstrate how the generated datasets can support comparisons of machine-learning models’ laundering-detection abilities. Public datasets give those comparisons a shared foundation instead of requiring access to private financial records.

A particular advantage is the completeness of the synthetic ground-truth labels. In real records, laundering that has never been detected can remain unlabeled, complicating evaluation. In generated data, the laundering labels are complete by construction. The paper argues that this can make synthetic data better for this aspect of model comparison, while the realism of the simulated transactions remains part of the generator’s design objective.
neurips-2023-realistic-synthetic-financi.tldr: An agent-based transaction generator supplies public anti-money-laundering benchmarks with complete labels and calibration toward realistic financial activity.

paragraphs: Some learning problems constrain their solutions to curved spaces called Riemannian manifolds. Stochastic gradient methods can optimize on these spaces, but without geodesic convexity, their behavior near undesirable stationary points needs justification. This paper investigates whether such methods avoid strict saddle points, where there remains a direction of improvement despite a vanishing gradient.

The analysis covers a family of retraction-based algorithms. These methods can have lower per-iteration costs than Riemannian gradient descent, and the family includes natural policy gradient methods and mirror descent in ordinary convex spaces. This broad formulation allows the result to apply beyond one particular manifold optimization routine.

Under mild assumptions on the manifold and the source of gradient information, the studied methods avoid strict saddle points and strict saddle submanifolds with probability one, from any initialization. This is an almost-sure avoidance guarantee under the stated conditions. It supports the use of stochastic manifold optimization by ruling out strict saddles as limiting outcomes in the analyzed setting, addressing a central obstacle to reaching local minima.
neurips-2023-riemannian-stochastic-optim.tldr: Under mild manifold and gradient-oracle assumptions, a broad family of stochastic Riemannian methods avoids strict saddles with probability one.

paragraphs: The Segment Anything Model supports flexible prompts and strong zero-shot segmentation, but its masks can miss fine details in objects with intricate structures. HQ-SAM aims to improve that mask quality while preserving the original model’s promptable design, efficiency, and ability to generalize to new segmentation settings.

The method preserves SAM’s pre-trained weights and adds a small number of trainable parameters. Its main addition is a learnable High-Quality Output Token inside the mask decoder, responsible for predicting the refined mask. The model also combines decoder features with early and final vision-transformer features to improve the detail available for mask prediction.

The added parameters are trained on 44,000 fine-grained masks assembled from several sources, with training reported to take four hours on eight GPUs. Evaluation spans ten segmentation datasets and different downstream tasks; eight datasets use a zero-shot transfer protocol. The results support improving detailed segmentation through targeted additions to an existing foundation model, with minimal extra parameters and computation.
neurips-2023-segment-anything-in-high-qu.tldr: HQ-SAM improves detailed segmentation by adding a learned output token and fused features while preserving SAM’s pre-trained weights.

paragraphs: Masked pre-training teaches a model by hiding part of its input and asking it to reconstruct the missing content. For time series, randomly removing observations can destroy the temporal variations that carry meaning. The resulting reconstruction problem can become too difficult to provide useful guidance for learning representations.

SimMTM reconstructs missing time points by combining information from multiple masked series. It uses a weighted aggregation of neighboring representations outside the underlying data manifold, assembling complementary temporal variations that survive in different masked inputs. The framework also learns local manifold structure, connecting reconstruction to the relationships among nearby examples.

The authors evaluate the learned representations through fine-tuning for forecasting and classification, covering both within-domain and cross-domain settings. They report state-of-the-art performance against the time-series pre-training methods compared. The findings support the idea that reconstructing from several complementary damaged views can make masked learning more useful for temporal data, where the pattern of change is central to what a model needs to understand.
neurips-2023-simmtm-a-simple-pre-trainin.tldr: SimMTM combines complementary masked time series to reconstruct temporal patterns, improving forecasting and classification after pre-training.

paragraphs: A language model may answer the same factual question differently when the wording changes. This makes a single prompt an incomplete test of how reliably the model can produce a fact. The paper introduces KaRR, a statistical assessment method that accounts for variation in how facts are queried.

KaRR estimates how likely the model is to generate text naming the answer entity under diverse prompts for a subject and relation, relative to generating it by chance. The assessment suite covers 994,123 entities, 600 relations, and 1,395,905 textual aliases. These aliases support evaluating factual knowledge across different textual expressions rather than relying on one surface form.

The authors evaluate 20 language models and report a Kendall rank correlation of 0.43 with human assessments. Within the same backbone architecture, their results show knowledge following a scaling law. They also find that instruction tuning sometimes reduces reliable factual generation. The findings distinguish instruction-following improvements from factual reliability and motivate assessing knowledge across prompt variations.
neurips-2023-statistical-knowledge-asses.tldr: KaRR measures factual knowledge across prompt variations, finding scaling trends within architectures and occasional losses in factual reliability after instruction tuning.

paragraphs: StressID is a dataset for studying stress identification using facial video, audio, and physiological measurements, either separately or together. A camera and microphone capture facial expressions and sound, while a wearable device records electrocardiography, electrodermal activity, and respiration. The collection setup synchronizes these sources so they can be analyzed as corresponding observations.

The dataset includes 65 participants completing eleven tasks and contains more than 39 hours of annotated recordings. Tasks use different kinds of stress-inducing stimuli, including emotional videos, mathematical or comprehension exercises, and public speaking. Participants also rate their perceived relaxation, stress, arousal, and valence, providing self-reported information alongside the recorded signals.

The paper supplies baseline stress-classification pipelines with cleaning, feature extraction, and classification stages for each modality. It also provides predictive models combining all three data sources. Together with the released data and baseline code, these components support comparisons between single-source and combined-source stress identification across a varied set of eliciting tasks.
neurips-2023-stressid-a-multimodal-datas.tldr: StressID provides synchronized facial, audio, and physiological recordings from 65 participants, plus baseline models for stress identification.

paragraphs: Symbol-LLM studies how symbolic reasoning can support understanding human activities in images. A symbolic system represents relevant concepts as symbols and connects them through rules. The paper argues that earlier systems were constrained by manually designed symbol sets and rules derived from visual annotations, limiting their coverage of complex activities and novel combinations.

The proposed method uses large language models as a source of symbols and rules. The aim is to approximate broad conceptual coverage and rational relationships without manually annotating a massive body of human knowledge. For an input image, the system extracts visual content, checks it against the symbols, and reasons about activity meaning through fuzzy-logic calculations.

The authors report superior performance across extensive activity-understanding tasks. The approach connects visual evidence to an explicit symbolic reasoning process, with language models supplying knowledge used by that process. Its stated contribution is a way to broaden the symbolic vocabulary and rule base available for activity reasoning, addressing the restricted coverage of earlier symbolic systems.
neurips-2023-symbol-llm-leverage-languag.tldr: Symbol-LLM uses language-model-derived symbols and rules with fuzzy logic to reason about human activities from visual evidence.

paragraphs: Generalization bounds describe how a learning algorithm’s performance on training data relates to its performance beyond that data. This paper sharpens such bounds for uniformly stable randomized algorithms within a PAC-Bayesian framework. Stability captures limited sensitivity to changes in the training sample, making it useful for analyzing generalization.

The key step is a tighter bound on the moment generating function of the generalization gap. The authors obtain it using concentration results for weakly dependent random variables. They introduce a sub-exponential assumption on the stability parameter, which provides a common framework for handling the randomness involved in the algorithms under study.

The resulting bounds improve earlier results by up to a factor of the square root of the sample size, ignoring a logarithmic factor. The authors instantiate the framework for stochastic gradient descent and randomized coordinate descent. Their results apply to nonsmooth convex problems and remove a previous strong-convexity requirement. This broadens the covered optimization settings while retaining the paper’s stated stability assumption.
neurips-2023-toward-better-pac-bayes-bou.tldr: Sharper PAC-Bayes bounds improve guarantees for stable randomized algorithms and cover nonsmooth convex problems without requiring strong convexity.

paragraphs: Machine-learned interatomic potentials can support atomistic simulations, but accurate training data require expensive reference calculations. This paper proposes transferring knowledge from a pre-trained graph neural network to system-specific catalytic processes. The goal is to reuse learned representations of chemical environments when fitting a new potential energy surface.

The method extracts a feature map from graph neural networks pre-trained on OC20 and combines it with kernel mean embeddings. These representations are then used to learn from datasets for the target system. The authors further modify the kernel to include chemical species information, reporting improvements in both predictive performance and interpretability.

Tests use realistic datasets of increasing complexity. The approach shows strong generalization and transferability, outperforming methods based on graph neural networks alone, ridge regression alone, and similar fine-tuning approaches. The findings support combining transferable neural features with a chemically informed kernel method to make better use of system-specific reference data for learning interatomic potentials.
neurips-2023-transfer-learning-for-atomi.tldr: Pre-trained graph-network features and chemically informed kernel mean embeddings improve transfer learning for catalytic potential energy surfaces.

paragraphs: Variational inference approximates a posterior distribution that is too difficult to compute directly using a simpler distribution. This paper develops an approach based on matching score functions, the gradients of log densities. Its starting principle is that equal distributions have equal scores at every point on their support.

At each iteration, the algorithm samples latent variables and minimally adjusts the current approximation to match the posterior’s score at that sample. When the approximation is Gaussian, this inner optimization has a closed-form solution. The resulting Gaussian score-matching method, GSM-VI, requires only a differentiable joint distribution, enabling application across a broad class of Bayesian models.

The authors examine sensitivity to dimensionality, covariance conditioning, and mismatch between the approximation and target. They also evaluate real-world inference problems from posteriorDB. Compared with black-box variational inference that optimizes the evidence lower bound, GSM-VI is faster and equally or more accurate in the reported experiments. Across a wide range of target posteriors, it reaches comparable approximation quality using 10–100 times fewer gradient evaluations.
neurips-2023-variational-inference-with-.tldr: Gaussian score-matching variational inference uses closed-form local updates and reaches comparable posterior approximation quality with substantially fewer gradient evaluations in reported experiments.
